rows.source: Building Safety Regulator high-rise residential safety
rows.verified: Accountable persons manage fire-spread and structural-failure risks in high-rise residential buildings.

rows.source: Building Safety Regulator high-rise residential safety
rows.verified: A high-rise residential building must be registered with the Building Safety Regulator before people live there.

rows.source: Building Safety Regulator high-rise residential safety
rows.verified: Residents should avoid creating or increasing building-safety risks and cooperate with accountable persons.

rows.source: Building Safety Regulator high-rise residential safety
rows.verified: The principal accountable person must operate and publish a building-safety complaints policy.

rows.source: Building Safety Regulator high-rise residential safety
rows.verified: Residents can complain about fire-spread or structural-failure risks and accountable-person performance.

rows.source: Building Safety Regulator high-rise residential safety
rows.verified: The principal accountable person must prepare and maintain a resident engagement strategy.

rows.source: Building Safety Regulator high-rise residential safety
rows.verified: Residents must receive specified information about responsible persons, engagement and relevant fire-safety management documents.

rows.source: Building Safety Regulator high-rise residential safety
rows.verified: A complaint can be referred to the Building Safety Regulator when the building process has not resolved it.

rows.source: Building Safety Regulator high-rise residential safety
rows.verified: Building-safety duties depend on building height and use, common parts, accountable-person roles, risk assessment and resident circumstances.

rows.source: Building Safety Regulator high-rise residential safety
rows.verified: High-rise safety evidence is building- and dutyholder-specific and is not an exact parcel-level fire or structural-failure probability.
